topic.title: Core Concepts
topic.shortdesc: Bookmaps, topic types, metadata mapping, and the transformation pipeline.

section.title: The Bookmap
section.p: A bookmapstructurebookmap is a specialized DITA map designed for book-like publications. It provides structural elements that map directly to the sections of a printed or digital book:

dlentry.dd: Contains the prefacepreface, forewordforeword, dedicationdedication, acknowledgments, and other introductory material. Each topicref in the frontmatter can carry a type attribute (preface, dedication, etc.) that the plugin uses to assign the correct DPUB-ARIA role.
The main body content. Chapters can contain nested topicrefs for sections and sub-sections. The plugin generates a hierarchical table of contents from this structure.

Contains appendixstructureappendices (via <appendices> and <appendix>), the colophon, and the <booklists> element, which triggers generation of the glossarygenerationglossary, indexgenerationindex, list of figures, and list of tables.

section.title: Topic Types
section.p: The plugin supports all standard topic typesDITA topic types. Each is rendered with the same XHTML template, but the topic's specialization is reflected in the epub:type and role attributes of the output:

ul.li: Topic — the generic base type, suitable for any content.
Concept — conceptual information, background, and overviews.
Reference — lookup material such as API documentation, parameter tables, or command references.
Glossentry — a term/definition pair. Glossentries referenced from a <glossarylist> are consolidated into a single alphabetized glossary page.

section.title: Metadata Mapping
section.p: The plugin extracts metadatamappingmetadata from the bookmap's <bookmeta> element and maps it to EPUB's Dublin Core and OPF metadata properties:

section.title: The Transformation Pipeline
section.p: The transformation proceeds in four phases:

ol.li: Pre-processing — DITA-OT resolves conrefs, keyrefs, and conditional attributes, producing a resolved temporary directory.
XSLT transformation — the plugin's XSLT 3.0 stylesheets process the resolved map and topics, generating OPF, navigation, and XHTML content documents.
Post-processing — Java utilities handle font obfuscation, image optimization, and CSS copying.
Packaging and validation — the output directory is packaged into a standards-compliant EPUB ZIP archive and optionally validated with EPUBCheck.

section.note: You can inspect the intermediate output by adding --clean-temp=no to the command line. The resolved DITA files will remain in the temporary directory.
